newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close at new high as rate fears ebb.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close at new high as rate fears ebb.

text.p: The Stockholm bourse ended at a new all-time high on Thursday, opening lower in line with a weaker close on Wall Street but reversing losses by midday as interest rate fears ebbed and with bond markets favourable.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.41 percent to 2,472.87 after shares worth 4.68 billion crowns changed hands.
"There is nothing that is holding it back," one London-based broker said.
"Interest rates are going in the right direction, the dollar is going in the right direction and there is a lot of activity on the mergers and acquisitions market."
A winner of the day was international engineer ABB that jumped 24 to 822 crowns on market rumours of a large order. The company denied any such order.

Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz announced plans to open its first five stores in Finland in the second half of 1997 but the share still slipped, falling 25 to 1,095 crowns, after posting hefty gains earlier this week.
The forestry sector was a loser, slipping 0.52 percent. MoDo said higher pulp prices were unlikely in quarter one this year and NorScan stocks were set to expand.
